screens.title: Workspace list
items: Back chevron. The destination is not shown.
Search, then a three-line list-options icon. Its menu is unopened.
Pinned and time/workspace groups. Rows pair task titles with project, execution/check status, and change totals.
Persistent rounded composer: plus on the left, prompt field in the middle, microphone on the right.
screens.lesson: Make status and the next action visible before the user opens a conversation.

screens.title: Voice and expanded composer
items: Rounded compose sheet with a centered drag handle; the list behind it is dimmed.
Repository and branch share a dropdown control.
Live transcription appears in the prompt field.
Plus, then model name and dropdown chevron.
Recording control combines a stop-shaped icon, elapsed time, and waveform. Final send behavior is not visible.
screens.lesson: Keep context, model selection, and input together while the keyboard is open.

screens.title: Image feedback
items: Close and trash icons. The exact target of deletion is unverified.
Image canvas with numbered comments and freehand red marks. The pictured Appearance screen belongs to the attached image, not Cursor settings.
Comment field with its point number at left and a checkmark at right.
screens.lesson: Attach feedback to an exact point so the agent knows which part of an image the user means.

screens.title: Finished conversation
items: Back on the left; overflow on the right.
User prompt, completion duration, then a walkthrough video with a centered play control and explanatory text.
Review with addition/deletion totals, followed by Squash & Merge.
Follow-up composer retains plus on the left and microphone on the right.
screens.lesson: Put evidence and follow-up input beside the action that finishes the work.

screens.title: Lock-screen activity
items: Status and task title above change totals and file count. Review sits at the lower right.
Active count above several task titles and elapsed times; additional tasks collapse into a count.
Flashlight and camera belong to iOS. They are not Cursor actions.
screens.lesson: A notification should tell the user what needs attention and provide a direct way back.

screens.title: Pull-request overview
items: Back on the left; clock-shaped and overflow controls on the right. Clock action unverified.
PR state, change totals, file count, and commit count.
Checks and reviewer avatars above the full-width Squash & Merge button.
Deployment rows include status and external-link arrows. Demo thumbnails follow. This screenshot does not show the file-diff screen.
screens.lesson: Show readiness evidence before the merge action. Do not infer a confirmation flow from a screenshot.

screens.title: iPad Inbox
items: Search, New Agent, Inbox, then task groups such as Needs Attention, Ready to Merge, and Open PR. Filter-shaped and sidebar controls sit at the top.
Four overview cards: All Agents, Working, Needs Attention, and In Review.
Workspace rows end in disclosure chevrons. Add Workspace is at the end.
Search and folder-plus controls. Their expanded views are unverified.
screens.lesson: Organize the home screen around work needing attention, with workspace grouping below.

screens.title: iPad annotation
items: Checkmark control to finish the editor.
Large image with freehand marks and numbered comment points.
Inline comment field and its own checkmark. Keyboard editing controls sit below it.
screens.lesson: Use the larger canvas for precise feedback while keeping the comment attached to its point.

screens.title: iPad review
items: Task navigation remains visible beside the PR.
Back on the left; link and overflow controls on the right. PR state, totals, title, and number appear below.
Checks, reviewer status, and a potential-issue row above a wide merge button. A summary follows.
screens.lesson: Keep conversation navigation available while the user inspects review evidence.

journeys.title: First run and start work
journeys.path: Install → sign in → choose repository and branch → write task → launch
journeys.detail: SSO applies when required. Run configuration can select a worker, model, and MCP servers. Exact first-run screens, selection menus, and launch-button location remain unverified.

journeys.title: Dictate a task
journeys.path: Bottom microphone → expanded composer → live transcript → finish recording → submit
journeys.detail: The published voice clip shows the composer above the keyboard and transcription updating. The final recording-to-submit transition is not shown in the sampled frames.

journeys.title: Give visual feedback
journeys.path: Attach image → mark a point or draw → add comment → finish annotation → send instruction
journeys.detail: Numbered points and inline comments are visible in the screenshots. The attachment-picker sequence and whether finishing the editor returns to a draft need live verification.

journeys.title: Follow a running agent
journeys.path: Open task → read progress → send follow-up → open child transcript when needed
journeys.detail: The docs support follow-ups during a run and opening subagent cards. Exact stop, retry, and failed-run controls have not been observed.

journeys.title: Leave and return
journeys.path: Start work → leave app → receive status change → reopen → catch up
journeys.detail: Completion, input needed, and ready-for-review notifications are documented. Cloud work continues independently of the phone. Notification destinations and unread behavior need a live check.

journeys.title: Review and finish
journeys.path: Completed task → Review → inspect evidence and checks → revise or merge
journeys.detail: Screenshots show the Review shortcut, PR readiness card, and merge action. Current review also includes comments, approvals, reviewer changes, and multiple PRs per conversation. Merge confirmation and blocked states are unverified.

journeys.title: Control work on the Mac
journeys.path: Desktop Settings > Agents → enable Remote Control → /remote-control → open the task on iPhone
journeys.detail: Keep the computer awake, online, and its workspace open. Team admin enablement can be required. The phone directs an existing desktop session.

journeys.title: Recover after disconnection
journeys.path: Return to app → reconnect and catch up → pull down Inbox if needed
journeys.detail: Streaming pauses in the background and resumes on return. If repositories are missing, connect source control on the web, refresh, then sign out and back in if necessary.

journeys.title: Use iPad for review
journeys.path: Inbox or sidebar task → conversation → adjacent review → comments or follow-up
journeys.detail: The July update adds sidebar chats, review beside chat, wider diffs, and Apple Pencil annotation. The supplied images show the controls; rotation and pane resizing are untested.

findings: Make connection setup the first complete journey
Nyte currently needs a reachable server URL and token. A phone companion is difficult to use away from the desk until pairing, host availability, and reconnection are clear.
Make the task list answer “what needs me?”

Show working, waiting for input, finished, and failed states clearly. Treat unread state and execution state separately. The suggested states are Nyte design recommendations, not a reconstruction of Cursor internals.
Nyte supports text send, streaming, and stop. Its README says answering approval prompts is missing. Let users resolve the situations that make them pick up the phone.
Keep the composer at the bottom
Use one consistent input location in the list and conversation. Expand it for context selection and attachments, with the keyboard visible.
Introduce useful tool results, files changed, and screenshots. A review shortcut belongs next to the follow-up composer when actionable output exists.
Preserve a useful screen without a connection
Nyte refreshes on return and retains failed drafts while a conversation is open. Persisted history and drafts would make intermittent phone use more dependable.
Keep runtime work on the host

Nyte already places credentials and execution on the Mac. Cursor’s documented Remote Control moves the agent loop to its cloud while tools stay on the computer. These are different architectures; similar UI does not require copying that split.
